## Goal

Document the herdr worklist hydrator in packages/herdr/README.md so operators understand its cadence, semantics, safety, and why pane-title IDs must survive truncation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README documents: 30s cadence, immediate run on focus-resume, visibility gating (zero wl while hidden).
2. README documents demotion rules (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open) with the status/stage compatibility note.
3. README documents fail-open semantics (missing/unparseable CLI output → no demotions, never a crash).
4. README documents the pane-title ID-survival rationale (matching relies on ' - WL-<id>' in titles; pane-title amendment F0).
5. Docs match the shipped implementation (reviewed at close).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/README.md

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a 'Hydrator' subsection under the worklist/downtime worker docs area with the bullets above.

## Dependencies

- Requires F2 (implementation facts) and F0 (format rationale)

# Measure the post-deploy benefit of mode-aware AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM

## Problem statement

WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME makes the downtime dispatcher pass a mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` to dispatched audit panes: `2` in cheap mode when a second local slot is genuinely free and the dispatch is single-flight, `1` otherwise. The config is now wired through the production spawn path, so the change can take effect after the `dev`→`main` release. Its measured benefit has not yet been observed: the work item cites only the pre-change 2026-08-22 baseline (local model busy ~25-38% during 04:00-06:00 cheap window) and the current values were taken with the config unwired (always `1`).

This item is the operational follow-up: capture the post-change measurement once the change is running overnight.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants to confirm the change actually raises cheap-window local utilisation without increasing remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-change proxy usage report for at least one 04:00-06:00 cheap window (after the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME release) recorded, showing the dispatched-audit Phase 2 children overlapping the parent.
2. Cheap-window local busy % compared against the 25-38% baseline and reported (up, flat, or down).
3. Remote fallback rate compared against the pre-change rate and reported (must not increase).
4. Dispatched-audit Phase 2 wall-clock (per audit, or median across audits) compared against the pre-change sequential mode and reported.
5. If the benefit is not observed (busy % flat/down, or fallback up), a follow-up work item is created with the finding and a proposed remedy.

## Notes

discovered-from:WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME

- Baseline: `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` (2026-08-22 04:00-06:00 cheap window, ~25-38% local busy).
- Method: run the proxy usage report over the target window; identify `audit-WL-*` sessions and their Phase 2 child sessions; compute overlap and busy %.
- Depends on the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME release reaching `main` (ship skill) and the mode-switch worker observing `cheap` mode during the window.
- This item is operational and assigned to the Operator; it does not block the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME code change.
data.title: Measure dispatched-audit Phase 2 overlap benefit after mode-aware PARALLELISM lands

data.description:
# Capture a cheap-mode dispatched audit to measure Phase 2 PARALLELISM benefit

discovered-from:WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5

## Finding

The mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` code is live in the running `dev` build
(herdr `dist/` rebuilt 2026-09-24 18:38 and contains the WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME wiring;
the running herdr checkout HEAD `e1bea036` includes `6188a90d`). A `dev`→`main`
release is **not** required for the change to take effect on this machine.

The first full post-change cheap window (2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) contained **no
dispatched audits** — the downtime dispatcher selected only implement/plan/intake/
scheduled items (last audit dispatch was 2026-09-24T23:54Z in fast mode; no
`audit-*` pi sessions started in the window). Because the PARALLELISM=2 path is
audit-only, it was never exercised, so the Phase 2 child-overlap / wall-clock
benefit is unmeasured.

Window-level proxy metrics (proxy host 192.168.0.199, via `proxy-usage-analysis`):

- Remote fallback: 41.7% (post, 2026-09-25 01:00-10:00) vs 52.8% (pre, 2026-09-24
  01:00-10:00) → down.
- Cheap-window busy: 67.7% (post) vs 67.7% (pre) → flat; per-hour 04:00-05:00
  25.2%, 05:00-06:00 77.0%.
- The 25-38% baseline cited in WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5 does not match the archived
  2026-08-22 report (04:00-05:00 49.9%, 05:00-06:00 55.4%) — reconcile which
  baseline is authoritative.

## Goal

As the operator, I want at least one dispatched audit to run during a cheap window so
I can measure whether mode-aware `PARALLELISM=2` makes its Phase 2 children overlap
the parent and shortens Phase 2 wall-clock, without raising remote fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At least one dispatched audit runs in a 01:00-10:00 cheap window, and
   `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` is confirmed on the audit pane (e.g. via
   `/proc/<pid>/environ`).
2. The proxy usage report for that window shows the audit's Phase 2 child sessions
   overlapping the parent (peak cheap-mode concurrency 2, not 1).
3. Phase 2 wall-clock for that audit is compared against a pre-change sequential
   audit and reported.
4. Remote fallback rate for that window does not increase vs the pre-change
   comparison.
5. Findings recorded on WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5.

## Proposed remedy (pick one)

- Prefer audit-tier work items for downtime dispatch during cheap windows, so the
  new path is actually exercised; or
- Trigger one manual audit during a cheap window and capture the spawn env plus the
  proxy report; or
- Extend the observation period until a dispatched audit lands in cheap mode.

## Notes

- Proxy logs/reports live on 192.168.0.199 (`/var/log/llama-proxy`,
  `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable over SSH from the ContextHub machine.
- Cheap window per the slot schedule is 01:00-10:00; the baseline focus was
  04:00-06:00.

data.comment:
Re-done correctly after operator correction. **The `dev`→`main` release is NOT required** — the running herdr build is from `dev` and already contains the change. Measurement outcome recorded; the specific audit benefit could not be exercised, so a child follow-up was created.

## Correction to the earlier blocker analysis

- The running herdr checkout HEAD is `e1bea036`, which **includes** `6188a90d` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 6188a90d HEAD` → yes).
- `packages/herdr/dist/` was rebuilt **2026-09-24 18:38** and `dist/downtime-worker.js` contains the `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` wiring. So the mode-aware spawn path is live on this machine without any release.
- The proxy logs/reports are not local: they live on the proxy host **192.168.0.199** (`/var/log/llama-proxy`, `~/proxy-usage-reports`), reachable via SSH. The earlier "no data" conclusion was wrong.

## Measured proxy data (proxy-usage-analysis on 192.168.0.199)

Post-change cheap window **2026-09-25 01:00-10:00** (first full cheap window after dist build 2026-09-24 18:38):

| Metric | Post (2026-09-25) | Pre (2026-09-24) | Cited baseline (2026-08-22) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remote fallback | 41.7% (821/1970) | 52.8% (1490/2821) | — |
| Cheap busy (overall) | 67.7% | 67.7% | 57.7% |
| 04:00-05:00 busy | 25.2% | 88.6% | 49.9% |
| 05:00-06:00 busy | 77.0% | 44.8% | 55.4% |
| Peak concurrency | 3 | 3 | 4 |

- The 25-38% baseline cited in this item does **not** match the archived `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-22/report.md` (which shows 49.9% / 55.4% for 04:00-06:00). The two-hour figures are noisy and workload-dependent; busy % is flat vs the same-week pre-change window.

## Critical finding: the mechanism was never exercised

**No audits were dispatched during the post-change cheap window.** The downtime dispatch log (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) shows only implement/plan/intake/scheduled dispatches between 2026-09-25 01:00-10:00; the last audit dispatch was 2026-09-24T23:54:50Z (fast mode), and no `audit-*` pi sessions started in 01:00-10:00. `PARALLELISM=2` only affects the audit path, so it had **zero** influence on the window — busy % differences are from non-audit work.

## AC verdicts

- **AC2 (busy % vs baseline)** — met: reported up/flat/down above (flat vs same-week pre-change; mixed vs the cited figures).
- **AC3 (fallback rate, must not increase)** — met: 41.7% vs 52.8% → decreased.
- **AC1 (report showing Phase 2 children overlapping the parent)** — unmet: no dispatched audit ran in the window, so no overlap exists to show.
- **AC4 (Phase 2 wall-clock vs sequential)** — unmet: no post-change cheap-mode audit to compare.
- **AC5 (follow-up if benefit not observed)** — done: **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** (child) captures the finding, the proposed remedy (prefer audit-tier dispatch in cheap windows / trigger one manual cheap-window audit / extend observation), and the measurement re-run criteria.

## Disposition

This item is blocked on WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA: once one dispatched audit runs in a cheap window, the Phase 2 overlap and wall-clock comparison can be completed here. Reset to `open` (stage `idea`), assignee Operator; `needsProducerReview` cleared (the path forward is defined by the child).
